---
description: "Use when changing the FUSE layer in component/libfuse: cgo callbacks, errno mapping, open file handles, native file I/O, fuse2 and fuse3 handlers."
applyTo: "component/libfuse/**"
---
# libfuse component

- `libfuse_handler.go` (fuse3, `//go:build !fuse2`) and `libfuse2_handler.go` (fuse2, `//go:build fuse2`) export the same set of callbacks, a few of them with a `libfuse2_` prefix, using each libfuse version's C signatures. Make the same change in both files and in their `*_test_wrapper.go` (built only with the `unittest` tag), then run `make check` (compiles both variants) and `make test FUSE=fuse2 PKG=./component/libfuse` in addition to the fuse3 tests.
- A callback runs on a libfuse thread through cgo. Return a negative errno instead of panicking, because a panic in a callback takes the mount down. Map an error with `errnoOf(err, <errnos the callback reports>...)` from `errno.go`, as the other callbacks do: it matches with `errors.Is`, so wrapped and joined errors work, and returns `EIO` for anything not in the list. Add an errno to a callback's list only when applications need to tell that case apart.
- Callbacks that take a path call `common.IsValidObjectName(name)` first and return `-C.EINVAL` for a rejected name; `libfuse_getattr` returns `-C.ENOENT` instead, because such a name can never exist. Keep the check in any new callback that takes a path.
- Open file handles: C memory must not hold Go pointers, so libfuse's file handles refer to `handlemap` handles by ID (see the "File handles" comment at the top of `libfuse_handler.go`). `fi.fh` of a directory is the `handlemap.HandleID`; `fi.fh` of a file points to a native `file_handle_t` whose `obj` field holds the ID. Add the handle to `handlemap` before `newFileHandle`; if `newFileHandle` fails, release the handle with `abandonFileHandle` and return `-C.ENOMEM`. Look handles up with `loadFileHandle` or `loadDirHandle` and return `-C.EBADF` when one isn't found. Only `libfuse_release` deletes the handle and frees the native object. `make test-race` enables checkptr, which aborts if a Go pointer is converted back from C memory.
- When `file_cache` holds a file locally, reads and writes are served in C on the cached file's descriptor and never reach the Go `libfuse_read` and `libfuse_write` callbacks. Native writes only set a dirty mark, which `flush`, `fsync` and `release` carry over to the handle with `markNativeWritesDirty`. Keep that call in any new path that decides whether to upload.
- `flush` can run several times for one `open` (after `dup`, `dup2` or `fork`); `release` runs once, after the last descriptor closes. Don't do final cleanup in `flush`.
- Update the health-monitor statistics with `libfuseStatsCollector.PushEvents` and `UpdateStats` as the neighboring callbacks do.
- `libfuse_bench_test.go` measures the read and write callbacks, through the pipeline and served natively, without a mount. CI compares them with the base of a change and fails on a slowdown of more than 10%, so run `make bench-libfuse` after changing those paths or `internal/handlemap`, and don't add allocations or `log.Info` and higher logging to them.
- Unit tests call the exported callbacks through the test wrappers with `internal.MockComponent` as the next component. Check behavior that users see through a real mount with `make test-loopback`.
